subject.title: fix: Kubernetes teardown preserves custom namespaces

question: Should `./scripts/k8s/deploy.sh --delete` permanently become safe resource-only teardown, with any whole-namespace removal exposed as a separate explicit operator action?
rationale: The issue establishes that the current default can destroy unrelated workloads, while the current documentation establishes full namespace deletion as an existing CLI contract. Choosing the long-term command semantics is a maintainer product and upgrade decision, not a mechanical correctness judgment.

options.title: Adopt safe default and add explicit destructive mode
options.body: Keep `--delete` resource-only and add a clearly documented opt-in command or flag for operators who intentionally want to remove the namespace.

options.title: Adopt safe default without compatibility mode
options.body: Treat namespace retention as the new teardown contract and document that namespace lifecycle is entirely operator-managed.

options.title: Retain full deletion semantics
options.body: Keep namespace deletion as the default and pursue a different workflow for shared namespaces, accepting that the reported destructive behavior remains on the existing command.

recommendation.title: Adopt safe default and add explicit destructive mode
recommendation.body: Keep `--delete` resource-only and add a clearly documented opt-in command or flag for operators who intentionally want to remove the namespace.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the proposed implementation context, though confirmation should come from a repository decision-maker familiar with the Kubernetes CLI contract.
